paragraphs.source_en: When the various laws governing the Imperial House and court nobles were being settled, Ieyasu had consulted Tenkai, and under Tenkai’s leadership the proposed statutes had been deliberated and revised time and again. These laws were intimately bound up with the government of the shogunate. If the shogunate’s government were deficient in the slightest degree, laws that sought to constrain the Imperial House and court nobles would invite suspicion of usurpation. It was perhaps because Tenkai had considered these matters that he understood so profoundly the weight of the responsibilities borne by Ieyasu and Hidetada.
